header.running_head: 3. The Rights and Duties of Muslims

blocks.tamil_translation: ﷺ was in my house, an old woman came. When the Prophet ﷺ asked, “Who are you?”, she said, “I am Juthamah Madaniyyah.” When the Prophet ﷺ asked, “How are you all? After us (after we came to Madinah), how was your condition?”, she said, “O Rasulullah, may my mother and father be sacrificed for you! We are all well”, and the old woman left. I asked (in surprise), “O Rasulullah, you gave that old woman so much importance and paid her so much attention!” The Prophet ﷺ said, “This old woman used to come and go to us in the lifetime of Khadijah (RA); maintaining old friendships is (a sign of) Iman.”

blocks.arabic_text: عَنْ اَبِيْ هُرَيْرَةَ ﵁ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ ﷺ: لَا يَفْرَكْ مُؤْمِنٌ مُؤْمِنَةً، اِنْ كَرِهَ مِنْهَا خُلُقًا رَضِيَ مِنْهَا آخَرَ اَوْ قَالَ غَيْرَهُ.
blocks.source_reference_arabic: رواه مسلم باب الوصية بالنساء رقم:٣٦٤٥
blocks.tamil_translation: Hazrat Abu Hurairah (RA) narrates that Rasulullah ﷺ said: “It is not the quality of a Mu'min husband to harbour dislike for his Mu'min wife. If one of her traits is disliked, another trait will be liked, will it not?”

blocks.text:
Explanation:- In this hadith the Prophet ﷺ has stated a beautiful, concise principle needed for life. Even if a person has bad qualities, he will surely also have some good qualities! Who can there be who has no bad trait at all, or no good trait at all? Therefore, one should look at the good things and not look at the bad things.
(Tarjuman-us-Sunnah)
